title: Silence and Language
premise: Oscar Vane, a translator whose childhood language is dissolving word by word, has spent decades keeping an inventory of everything her family never said. When Mirela, the last fluent speaker of a dying language, offers to teach one final student, Oscar seizes the lessons as both rescue and excavation — and discovers the language holds the family's buried secret: what happened the winter her mother stopped speaking to her brother. As Mirela's memory fails and the family closes ranks around its arranged silence, Oscar must choose between loyalty to the living and fidelity to the truth, finally asking the forbidden question aloud. The novel ends with her mother's fragmented answer, a partial reconciliation, and Oscar translating the confession into the dying language so it survives somewhere beyond the family.
about_author: Q. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former court interpreter who spent fifteen years rendering other people's truths in borrowed words before turning to fiction. They live near a coastal archive of endangered languages and write at dawn, when the dictionaries are still asleep.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She catalogs the words her childhood language has lost to her — and, in a parallel notebook, the sentences her family has never spoken. A routine translation job collapses when she reaches for a word that isn't there anymore. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as professional composure.

chapters.title: The Last Speaker
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Mirela, ninety-one and sharp-tongued, interviews three applicants for her final apprenticeship and dismisses them all — then keeps Oscar waiting past her slot on purpose. Their first lesson is not vocabulary but listening. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two women guarding different silences.

chapters.title: Borrowed Words
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with letters from her mother interspersed. Lessons deepen; Mirela teaches through objects and omissions rather than grammar. Oscar notices Mirela flinches at one family name — her uncle's. Emotional beat: the thrill of learning shadowed by the first crack of intrusion.

chapters.title: What the Family Arranged
chapters.summary: Oscar's brother Daniel's POV. At a Sunday lunch, the family performs its choreography of avoidance around the absent uncle. Daniel privately warns Oscar that her lessons are 'stirring things Mother can't afford to lose.' Emotional beat: love expressed as enforcement; duty wearing loyalty's face.

chapters.title: The Winter Word
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Mirela, mid-lesson, produces a word with no polite translation — one tied to an accusation — and admits she knew Oscar's mother before the silence began. Her memory slips for the first time mid-sentence. Emotional beat: hunger for truth colliding with guilt over exploiting a failing mind.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Translated
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. He confronts Oscar with the family's version of the winter: a protection, not a betrayal. His account is loving, plausible, and slightly wrong, and Oscar catches the error only because of a new word Mirela taught her. Emotional beat: the seduction of a merciful lie.

chapters.title: Mirela Forgets the River
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mirela loses the word for river and, with it, whole afternoons of memory; Oscar begins recording sessions secretly, ashamed. The mother, sensing the end, sends a single sentence in the old language — her first in forty years. Emotional beat: grief outrunning curiosity; tenderness inside deception.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. With Mirela's lucidity failing and the family converging to stop the lessons, Oscar asks the forbidden question directly — in the dying language, so it cannot be pretended away. Mirela answers with the accusation, and names Oscar's mother as witness, not culprit. Emotional beat: climax; the relief and wreckage of speech.

chapters.title: Everything Unsaid
chapters.summary: Mother's POV, fragmentary and memory-broken. She gives Oscar the true account of the winter — her brother's act, her chosen silence as penance and shield. Daniel listens at the door and does not interrupt. Emotional beat: sorrow without absolution; love surviving the truth it was protecting.

chapters.title: A Language With Two Speakers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Mirela dies in early spring; at the funeral Oscar speaks the eulogy in the old language, including the family's confession, now carried outside the bloodline. She and her mother begin lessons together, clumsy and forgiving. Emotional beat: resolution — language outliving silence, love rebuilt on truth instead of duty.
